#+TITLE: Non-overlapping CLOCK lines

Every CLOCK line here is canonical AND no two of them share an
instant. ``clock overlap`` must report nothing and exit 0.

* Back-to-back tasks
:PROPERTIES:
:TASK_REF: 1
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-01-07 Wed 09:00 +0100]--[2026-01-07 Wed 10:00 +0100] =>  1:00
CLOCK: [2026-01-07 Wed 10:00 +0100]--[2026-01-07 Wed 11:00 +0100] =>  1:00
CLOCK: [2026-01-07 Wed 11:00 +0100]--[2026-01-07 Wed 12:00 +0100] =>  1:00
:END:

Adjacency is the normal clock-out/clock-in shape: the shared
boundary instant belongs to neither interval.

* Separated by gaps
:PROPERTIES:
:TASK_REF: 2
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-01-07 Wed 14:00 +0100]--[2026-01-07 Wed 15:30 +0100] =>  1:30
CLOCK: [2026-01-07 Wed 16:00 +0100]--[2026-01-07 Wed 17:00 +0100] =>  1:00
:END:

* Same wall-clock text, different zones
:PROPERTIES:
:TASK_REF: 3
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-01-08 Thu 09:30 +0800]--[2026-01-08 Thu 10:30 +0800] =>  1:00
CLOCK: [2026-01-08 Thu 09:30 +0100]--[2026-01-08 Thu 10:30 +0100] =>  1:00
:END:

These look identical but are seven hours apart as instants
(01:30Z versus 08:30Z), so they do not overlap.

* Zero-length clock inside a long one
:PROPERTIES:
:TASK_REF: 4
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-01-09 Fri 09:00 +0100]--[2026-01-09 Fri 18:00 +0100] =>  9:00
CLOCK: [2026-01-09 Fri 12:00 +0100]--[2026-01-09 Fri 12:00 +0100] =>  0:00
:END:

A zero-length interval spans no instant, so it cannot conflict
with anything. Whether it is *meaningful* is another rule's
problem.

* Running clock, ignored entirely
:PROPERTIES:
:TASK_REF: 5
:END:
:LOGBOOK:
CLOCK: [2026-01-10 Sat 09:00 +0100]
CLOCK: [2026-01-10 Sat 09:30 +0100]--[2026-01-10 Sat 10:30 +0100] =>  1:00
:END:

An open range has no end instant and is skipped, so it never
conflicts with the closed clock that follows it.
